title: Exploring the Frontiers of LLMs in Psychological Applications: A Comprehensive Review

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing studies that test LLMs with prompts designed to assess psychological heuristics (e.g., anchoring, representativeness, availability, framing effect) and comparing their responses to human decision-making patterns.

Reviewing studies that compare LLM responses on psychological scales to cross-cultural human data to identify overrepresentation of WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) perspectives and evaluate Eastern vs. Western cognitive traits.
Reviewing literature that uses network science (e.g., Behavioral Forma Mentis Networks) and language generation tasks to analyze semantic associations and biases toward math and STEM fields.

Summarizing literature that evaluates the propagation of harmful ideas, discrimination, and unfairness in downstream applications, such as reinforcing sexism in job advertisement translations and resume evaluations.
